rv.q: It is an important play that should be seen.
That Howard Skora's latest World Premiere is as entertaining as a fact-based play can be is icing on the rainbow-colored cake.

Texas Sodomy wants to be a raucous comedy, courtroom procedural, domestic tragedy, history pageant, and inspirational drama at once. Skora, who also directs, has found no theatrical language capable of holding them together.
Beautifully written, sublimely performed and flawlessly produced, Texas Sodomy is yet another Howard Skora triumph, as if I would expect anything less from this brilliant mind.
Howard Skora's world premiere transforms a landmark Supreme Court case into a deeply human theatrical experience without sacrificing humor or emotional complexity.

cn.t: Critics largely praise Howard Skora's fact-based drama about Lawrence v. Texas as entertaining and deeply human, though one reviewer finds the theatrical treatment superficial for such a landmark Supreme Court case.
